title: Quasi-finite morphisms
statement:
Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated, quasi-finite morphism of finite
type of $k_0$-schemes, with $Y_0$ quasi-separated of finite type over
$k_0$. Then $R^if_{0!}F=0$ for every Weil sheaf $F$ and every $i>0$;
and if $F$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w$ (resp. has all local
Frobenius eigenvalues of weight at most $w$), then so is (resp. has)
$f_{0!}F=R^0f_{0!}F$.

proof.text: The target $Y_0$ is quasi-compact because it is of finite type over a field, and is quasi-separated by hypothesis. Apply [thm-pqf-zmt-factorization] to obtain $X_0\xrightarrow{j_0}T_0\xrightarrow{p_0}Y_0$, with $j_0$ quasi-compact open, $p_0$ finite, and $f_0=p_0j_0$. This is a compactification since a finite morphism is proper [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. It is over $k_0$, giving compatible geometric base changes. No absolute separatedness of $Y_0$ or $T_0$ is inferred. The false inference in the blueprint proof of lem-zl-quasi-finite is avoided: the identity of the affine line with doubled origin is a finite morphism whose source is not separated over $k_0$. The compact-support operation of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] depends on a chosen compactification; by the comparison stated in [def-zl-weil-compact-support-cohomology] (for two compactifications of $f_0$, with no separatedness of $X_0,Y_0$ assumed, the higher images $R^n_cf_!F$ are isomorphic as Weil sheaves), every assertion of the item for an arbitrary compactification follows from the same assertion for $c_0=(j_0,p_0)$: vanishing, punctual bounds and mixedness are invariant under isomorphism of Weil sheaves. Steps 3-10 compute with $c_0$.

source.place: first paragraph, finite compactification; correction of the false absolute-separatedness inference

proof.text: For each affine open $V_0\subseteq Y_0$, put $T_{V_0}=T_0\times_{Y_0}V_0$ and $X_{V_0}=X_0\times_{Y_0}V_0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence], $p_{V_0}:T_{V_0}\to V_0$ is finite and $T_{V_0}$ is affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], $j_{V_0}:X_{V_0}\hookrightarrow T_{V_0}$ is open. Both $V_0$ and $T_{V_0}$ are separated over $k_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]; $X_{V_0}$ is separated over $k_0$ because its diagonal is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $T_{V_0}$. These schemes are finite type over $k_0$: $Y_0$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], its open $V_0$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] and locally finite type, $T_{V_0}$ is finite over $V_0$, and $X_{V_0}$ is a quasi-compact open of $T_{V_0}$. Their geometric base changes remain separated and finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. The affine opens cover $Y_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis].

source.place: finite factorization, restricted to affine target opens before applying separated-scheme results

proof.text: For $V=V_0\times_{k_0}k$, put $u:X_V\hookrightarrow X$ and $v:V\hookrightarrow Y$. The four schemes and the finite compactification scheme $T$ are Noetherian and finite-dimensional by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]; $\ell$ is invertible. Apply [lem-zl-framework-pbc-open-exchange-comparison] to the supplied finite compactification. It identifies the actual framework functor $R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_n Rp_{*,n}j_!K_n$ with the completed PBC $Rp_*j_!$ under the coefficient-presentation equivalences $J$. For the two composite functors it supplies the specified endpoint isomorphisms $S,T$ and the equation $\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{pbc}}J\circ S=T\circ J(\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{sf}})$. Thus the exchange comparison includes the strict quotient transitions and the proper/open mates before taking the derived limit. This is the comparison of functors and arrows needed here; equality of their finite evaluations alone is not used.

source.place: Common-stage compact-support exchange, with its previously missing framework/PBC comparison exposed as a separate lemma

proof.text: Apply [thm-cbc-qbar] to $J_XF$ in the PBC common-stage category. The hypotheses of its finite-stage theorem [thm-cbc-finite-extension] were checked in Step 3; these hypotheses impose relative separatedness of $f$, without absolute separatedness of $X,Y$. Its specified exchange $\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{pbc}}$ is invertible. The equation in Step 3 expresses $J(\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{sf}})=T^{-1}\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{pbc}}J\,S$, so the equivalence $J$ reflects invertibility and gives $v^*Rf_!F\simeq Rf_{V!}u^*F$ for the framework functors. The comparison lemma also identifies their Weil structures. Explicitly, the two pastings of the open square with geometric Frobenius are the same square, because $V_0$ and the compactification are over $k_0$. Identity/pasting coherence of the specified exchange in [thm-cbc-finite-extension] makes the composites equal; compose this equation with the image of the Weil arrow of $F$. Naturality of $S,T$ under the semilinear diagram isomorphisms gives the same equality in the framework category. Hence this is an isomorphism of Weil complexes, using [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex].

source.place: Common-stage base change and compatibility with the geometric-Frobenius square

proof.text: On the separated finite-type schemes of Step 2, the composition and properness laws of [prop-functor-package] give $Rf_{V!}\simeq Rp_{V*}j_{V!}$. Clause (2) of [lem-zl-immersion-weil-local-behavior] identifies the open compact-support operation with the exact $j_{V!}$ on constructible Weil sheaves, without any assumption on a coefficient embedding. The finite direct image is standard-$t$-exact and exact on the constructible heart by [lem-zl-finite-adic-direct-image]. Consequently for every constructible Weil sheaf $A$ on $X_{V_0}$, $Rf_{V!}A\simeq p_{V*}j_{V!}A$ is a sheaf in degree zero, and $A\mapsto p_{V*}j_{V!}A$ is exact. Every invocation of these three statements is now on absolutely separated finite-type schemes, including $T_{V_0}$ and its geometric base change.

source.place: proof of (1), exactness after affine target restriction

proof.text: Restriction to $V$ commutes with cohomology and is exact on constructible hearts by [lem-a1-constructible-pullback-t-exact]. Steps 4 and 5 therefore show that every cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^i(Rf_!F)$ with $i\ne0$ restricts to zero on each $V$. The restrictions form compatible local-heart data: for nested opens, the transition isomorphisms are the restrictions of the same global object, and their identity and cocycle equations are the restriction/pasting equations of Step 4. The open-cover exactness criterion in [lem-dl-a1-constructible-fibres-exact] detects its vanishing: apply it to the short complex $0\to\mathcal H^i(Rf_!F)\to0$, which is exact on each member of this separated open cover. Thus $Rf_!F$ lies in the constructible heart, and in particular $R^if_{0!}F=0$ for $i>0$. For any short exact sequence of constructible Weil sheaves on $X_0$, restriction to $X_V$ is exact by the pullback statement. By Step 5 its direct-image sequence is exact over each $V$. Applying the same open-cover criterion to that sequence proves that $f_{0!}=R^0f_{0!}$ is an exact functor globally. These checks are on constructible adic sheaves, not arbitrary pro-etale sheaves.

source.place: proof of (1), local detection of vanishing and exactness on a possibly nonseparated target

proof.text: Fix the arbitrary field embedding $\iota:\Omega\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$ of [sk-d-dl-general-weights]; no surjectivity is assumed. Suppose $F$ has punctual upper bound $w$, or is punctually pure of weight $w$, in the eigenvalue sense spelled out there. Restrict to $X_{V_0}$. A closed point of this open is closed in $X_0$: on both finite-type schemes this means its residue field is finite over $k_0$ by [lem-kun-closed-point-field]. Its stalk and local Frobenius are unchanged. Clause (2) of [lem-zl-immersion-weil-local-behavior] says that $B=j_{V!}(F|_{X_V})$ has that identical stalk and local Frobenius on $X_{V_0}$, and zero stalk elsewhere in $T_{V_0}$. Thus $B$ has the same bound or purity for this very embedding $\iota$. This uses the weight-free stalk assertion, not a weight-preservation theorem stated only for an isomorphism with $\mathbf C$.

source.place: Paragraph (2), open-immersion stalk argument; applied using the weight-free immersion statement and the original arbitrary embedding

proof.text: Fix closed $y\in V_0$, set $k_y=\kappa(y)$, and put $Z_0=T_{V_0}\times_{V_0}\operatorname{Spec}k_y$. The natural finite-fibre formula of [lem-zl-finite-adic-direct-image] identifies $(p_{V*}B)_{\bar y}$ with $H^0(Z,B|_Z)$, including its Frobenius action by the stated semilinear naturality. The fibre is finite, hence proper, so this is also $H_c^0$ by the properness law of [prop-functor-package]. Give $B|_Z$ the Weil arrow $\theta_B^{[d_y]}$, where $d_y=[k_y:k_0]$, and apply [lem-a1-finite-weil-sections-decomposition] over $k_y$, with algebraic closure $k$. For $x\in|Z_0|$, it gives a block of $e=[\kappa(x):k_y]$ summands on which $F_y$ acts cyclically and $F_y^e$ on each summand is $F_x$. The same-residue-field case of [lem-fd-weil-pullback-local-frobenius] for $Z_0\to T_{V_0}$ identifies its stalk operators over $k_0$. Over $k_y$, $e$ iterations of $\theta_B^{[d_y]}$ give $\theta_B^{[ed_y]}$, exactly the original $F_x$ of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. The point $x$ is closed in $T_{V_0}$, and $q_x=q_y^e$ because a $k_y$-basis of the degree-$e$ residue extension identifies its underlying set with $k_y^e$. If $\beta$ is an eigenvalue on this block, choose an eigenvector and a nonzero stalk component. The equation $F_y^ev=\beta^ev$ on that component shows that $\alpha=\beta^e$ is an eigenvalue of $F_x$. For the bound, multiplicativity of the given embedding and the complex absolute value gives $|\iota(\beta)|^e=|\iota(\alpha)|\le q_x^{w/2}=(q_y^{w/2})^e$. Taking the positive $e$-th root proves $|\iota(\beta)|\le q_y^{w/2}$. For purity use equality throughout. This works for every real $w$ and uses no surjectivity of $\iota$.

source.place: Closed-point finite-stalk formula and Frobenius orbit calculation from the paragraph beginning "It remains to check" through the displayed absolute-value equation; same calculation with inequalities for an upper bound, using only multiplicativity of the original embedding

proof.text: By Steps 4 and 5, $p_{V*}B$ is the restriction of $f_{0!}F$ to $V_0$, as a Weil sheaf. Every closed point of $Y_0$ is in an affine $V_0$, with the same residue field, stalk and local Frobenius as on $Y_0$. Thus Steps 7 and 8 show that $f_{0!}$ preserves punctual upper bounds and punctual purity globally for the original arbitrary embedding. There is no assertion about descent of local mixed filtrations; the punctual predicates are exactly the closed-point eigenvalue inequalities/equalities of [sk-d-dl-general-weights].

source.place: Unit proof paragraph: the sentences on Frobenius orbits, q_x=q_y^e, agreement of normalized weights and preservation of purity; checked on affine target opens

proof.text: If $F$ is mixed of weights at most $w$, choose its global finite filtration $0=G_0\subset\cdots\subset G_n=F$ with punctually pure quotients $Q_i$ of weights $u_i\le w$, as in [sk-d-dl-general-weights]. Exactness from Step 6 sends each $0\to G_{i-1}\to G_i\to Q_i\to0$ to $0\to f_{0!}G_{i-1}\to f_{0!}G_i\to f_{0!}Q_i\to0$. Thus the inclusions give a finite filtration of $f_{0!}F$ with quotients $f_{0!}Q_i$. Step 9 shows that these quotients are punctually pure of the same $u_i$. This is exactly the mixed upper bound $w$ of [sk-d-dl-general-weights]. A zero quotient can be omitted. In particular this argument applies one global input filtration; it does not assume descent or uniqueness of independently chosen local mixed filtrations.

source.place: final mixed-filtration paragraph, using global exactness and purity established above

lean.statement: theorem sfQuasiFiniteCompactSupport (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p) (Ω : Type v) [Field Ω] [Algebra (Padic l) Ω] [IsAlgClosure (Padic l) Ω] {X₀ Y₀ : Over (Spec (.of D.k₀))} [LocallyOfFiniteType X₀.hom] [QuasiCompact X₀.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType Y₀.hom] [QuasiCompact Y₀.hom] [QuasiSeparated Y₀.hom] (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀) [IsSeparated f₀.left] (_hqf : Scheme.Hom.IsQuasiFinite f₀.left) (c : Compactification f₀.left) (F : sfCommonStageWeilSheaf D l hl X₀ Ω) : (∀ i : ℕ, 0 < i → IsZero (zlWeilHigherShriek D l hl Ω f₀ c i F)) ∧ ∀ (iota : Ω →+* ℂ) (w : ℝ), (SfIsMixedOfWeightsAtMost D l hl Ω X₀ iota F w → SfIsMixedOfWeightsAtMost D l hl Ω Y₀ iota (zlWeilHigherShriek D l hl Ω f₀ c 0 F) w) ∧ ((∀ (x : {x : X₀.left // x ∈ closedPoints X₀.left}) (α : Ω), SfPunctualEigenvalue D l hl Ω X₀ F x α → ‖iota α‖ ≤ (Nat.card (X₀.left.residueField x.val) : ℝ) ^ (w / 2)) → ∀ (y : {y : Y₀.left // y ∈ closedPoints Y₀.left}) (β : Ω), SfPunctualEigenvalue D l hl Ω Y₀ (zlWeilHigherShriek D l hl Ω f₀ c 0 F) y β → ‖iota β‖ ≤ (Nat.card (Y₀.left.residueField y.val) : ℝ) ^ (w / 2))
